ui.import.replay.notFound: {id} is the replay's code from the link.
ui.import.replay.loadError: {id} is the replay's code; {status} is a web error code such as 500.
ui.import.results.pokedataError: Pokédata is a tournament results website. {status} is a web error code.
ui.import.rk9.noResponse: RK9 is a tournament website. {status} is a web error code.
ui.import.rk9.notRoster: RK9 is a tournament website; a roster is the list of players.
ui.import.standingsPhoto.noTable: TOM = Tournament Operations Manager, Play! Pokémon's event software; “Standings” is the name of one of its reports.
ui.import.standingsPhoto.noTableImage: TOM = Tournament Operations Manager; “Standings” is the name of one of its pages.
ui.import.standingsPhoto.retryLight: Progress text while reading a photo.
ui.import.standingsPhoto.straightening: Progress text while reading a photo.
ui.import.standingsPhoto.findingTable: Progress text while reading a photo.
ui.import.standingsPhoto.readingNames: Progress text while reading a photo.
ui.import.standingsPhoto.readingRecords: Progress text while reading a photo; 'records' are win-loss records.
ui.import.standingsPhoto.doubleChecking: Progress text while reading a photo.
ui.import.standingsPhoto.missingRows: Warning. {seen} is how many rows the page seems to have; {read} how many were read.
ui.import.standingsPhoto.noRecordWarning: Warning. {count} is the number of rows whose win-loss record couldn't be read.
ui.import.screenshot.noCards: 'Moves & More' is the name of a screen in Pokémon Champions; use the game's own name. 'Six' is the number of Pokémon on a team.
ui.import.screenshot.noMoves: 'Moves & More' and 'Stats' are names of screens in Pokémon Champions; use the game's own names.
ui.import.teamSheet.heic: HEIC is a photo file format used by iPhones; JPEG is another. Photos and AirDrop are iPhone features: use the phone's own names.
ui.import.teamSheet.finding: Progress text while reading a team list photo.
ui.import.teamSheet.turning: Progress text: the picture is being rotated.
ui.import.teamSheet.readingMon: Progress text; {n} is the current Pokémon and {total} the number on the sheet.
ui.import.teamSheet.readingTable: Progress text; {lang} is a language code such as EN or FR (Regionals sheets list every language).
ui.import.teamSheet.pageOf: Progress text while reading a PDF; {p} is the current page.
ui.import.teamSheet.pageStatus: Progress text; {status} is another progress message such as “Finding the team list boxes…”.
ui.import.teamSheet.genderMoves: Note under a Pokémon. {gender} is Male or Female (guessed from the moves).
ui.import.teamSheet.genderMovesUnsure: Same, when the guess is uncertain. {gender} is Male or Female.
ui.import.teamSheet.genderMissing: Note under a Pokémon whose gender wasn't written on the sheet.
ui.teamBattle.notReplay: Showdown (Pokémon Showdown) is a battle simulator website.
ui.teamBattle.setNotFinished: {score1} and {score2} are the games won by each player so far. The dash is an en dash.
term.format.reg2026MC: Official name of a VGC battle format (a season and its ruleset). Shown in the format dropdown and on graphics.
term.format.reg2026MB: Official name of a VGC battle format (a season and its ruleset). Shown in the format dropdown and on graphics.
term.format.reg2026MA: Official name of a VGC battle format (a season and its ruleset). Shown in the format dropdown and on graphics.
term.format.reg2025J: Official name of a VGC battle format (a season and its ruleset). Shown in the format dropdown and on graphics.
term.format.reg2025I: Official name of a VGC battle format (a season and its ruleset). Shown in the format dropdown and on graphics.
term.format.reg2025H: Official name of a VGC battle format (a season and its ruleset). Shown in the format dropdown and on graphics.
term.format.reg2024G: Official name of a VGC battle format (a season and its ruleset). Shown in the format dropdown and on graphics.
term.format.reg2025F: Official name of a VGC battle format (a season and its ruleset). Shown in the format dropdown and on graphics.
term.format.custom: Option for a format that isn't in the list; the person then types its name.
term.type.normal: Pokémon type name (shown in the Tera type dropdown). Use the official Spanish name.
gfx.common.tournament: Default title when no tournament name is typed. Printed on many styles, often in capitals.
gfx.common.playerN: Default name of a player with no name; {n} is 1 or 2.
gfx.common.topN: Small tag in a graphic's header, often printed in capitals; {count} is the number of players shown (4, 8…).
gfx.common.champion: Label on the winner's panel or banner; often printed in capitals.
gfx.common.topCut: Tag in a graphic's header: the players who made the elimination rounds. Often in capitals.
gfx.arena.kicker: Small line above the title on the Arena styles, printed in capitals; {count} is the number of players shown.
gfx.bracket.tbd: Placeholder for a bracket spot with no player yet (to be decided). Must stay short.
gfx.bracket.quarterfinals: Column heading over the first round of an 8-player bracket; printed in capitals.
gfx.bracket.semifinals: Column heading over the second round; printed in capitals.
gfx.bracket.finals: Column heading over the last round; printed in capitals.
gfx.bracket.roundN: Column heading for a round without a special name; {n} is the round number.
gfx.bracket.championStar: Label on the winner's box in the bracket; the stars are decoration.
gfx.bracket.empty: Shown on the graphic when no bracket has been entered. “Top cut bracket” and Standings are names on the website; keep them in step with ui.bracket.title and ui.app.tab.standings.
gfx.editorial.finalStandings: Small heading at the top of the Editorial style; printed in capitals.
gfx.eras.dexNo: Pokédex entry number, e.g. No.003; {n} is a 3-digit number.
gfx.eras.championTrainer: Category label on the Pokédex champion graphic.
gfx.eras.winLoss: Win/loss record on the Game Boy style; {record} is e.g. 6-2-0.
gfx.eras.championLine: Game Boy style dialogue line, imitating the old game's text box. {name} is the winner's name, already in capitals.
gfx.eras.newChampion: Game Boy style dialogue line when there is no winner name.
gfx.eras.rec: Abbreviation of Record, on the Pokédex and trading-card styles. Max 4 characters.
gfx.eras.soc: Abbreviation of Social (social media handle), on the Pokédex style. Max 4 characters.
gfx.eras.fld: Abbreviation of Field (number of players), on the Pokédex style. Max 4 characters.
gfx.eras.fmt: Abbreviation of Format, on the Pokédex style. Max 4 characters.
gfx.eras.players: Number of players in the event, on the Pokédex and trading-card styles.
gfx.eras.dexText: Sentence in the Pokédex style. {name} is the winner (or 'This trainer'), {tournament} the event (or 'the tournament'), {date} the date, {record} their record (or 'undefeated').
gfx.eras.dexTextNoDate: Same sentence when the event has no date.
gfx.eras.thisTrainer: Stands in for the winner's name in the Pokédex sentence.
gfx.eras.theTournament: Stands in for the event's name in the Pokédex sentence.
gfx.eras.undefeated: Stands in for the winner's record in the Pokédex sentence.
gfx.usage.title: Big title of the usage graphic.
gfx.usage.teamsCounted: Part of the facts line under the title; {count} is the number of teams the usage is based on.
gfx.usage.rank: Rank of a Pokémon on the usage graphic, e.g. #1.
gfx.vsResult.bestOf: In the header of the match graphic; {bestOf} is 3 or 5.
gfx.vsResult.bestOfGames: Same, plus {games}, the number of games played.
gfx.vsResult.vs: Between the two player names; printed in capitals.
gfx.vsResult.wins: Banner at the bottom of the match graphic; {name} is the winner.
gfx.vsResult.matchResult: Banner when there is no winner or round name.
gfx.tradingCard.competitor: What the Event Results trading card calls the player (the standings card says Champion). Shown on a card, so keep it short.
gfx.tradingCard.strip: Gold strip on the Classic trading card. {role} is Champion or Competitor; {type} is the event type (or 'Tournament').
gfx.tradingCard.stripPlayers: Same strip when the player count is known; {count} is the number of players.
gfx.tradingCard.holding: Text after a Pokémon's name on the Classic card; {item} is the held item. Starts with a space.
gfx.tradingCard.weakness: Trading-card field label, as on the real cards.
gfx.tradingCard.resistance: Trading-card field label, as on the real cards.
gfx.tradingCard.retreatCost: Trading-card field label (Classic card), as on the real cards.
gfx.tradingCard.retreat: Trading-card field label (Modern card), as on the real cards.
gfx.tradingCard.defaultFacts: Fills the card's flavor text when there are no event details.
gfx.tradingCard.flavor: Flavor text at the bottom of the card. {facts} is the event name, type and date; {format} and {cp} are the next two strings (they start with spaces, or are empty).
gfx.tradingCard.flavorFormat: Part of the flavor text; {format} is the format name. Starts with a space.
gfx.tradingCard.flavorCpClassic: Part of the Classic card's flavor text; {cp} is the Championship Points earned. Starts with two spaces.
gfx.tradingCard.flavorCpModern: Part of the Modern card's flavor text; {cp} is the Championship Points earned. Starts with a space.
gfx.tradingCard.illus: 'Illustrator' credit on the card; {social} is the player's social media handle.
gfx.tradingCard.no: Card number on the Modern card. Printed in capitals.
gfx.tradingCard.championOf: Strip on the Modern card; {type} is the event type (or 'Tournament').
gfx.tradingCard.roleAt: Same strip for Event Results; {role} is Competitor.
gfx.tradingCard.players: On the Modern card; {count} is the number of players.
gfx.teamBattle.title: Name of the team match graphic; used as a heading or small kicker.
gfx.teamBattle.victory: Big tag on the team battle win graphics; often in capitals.
gfx.teamBattle.final: Big tag on the team battle loss graphics; often in capitals.
gfx.teamBattle.season: Under a team's name; {record} is its season record, e.g. 4-1.
gfx.teamBattle.teamA: Default name of the first team.
gfx.teamBattle.teamB: Default name of the second team.
gfx.teamBattle.yourTeam: Default name of the posting team.
gfx.teamBattle.winScore: Headline when the posting team won, e.g. “Wolves win 4–2”. {team} is the team's name; the dash is an en dash.
gfx.teamBattle.fallScore: Headline when the posting team lost, e.g. “Wolves fall 2–4”. {team} is the team's name.
gfx.teamBattle.winLine: Short line when the posting team won. {team} is the team's name.
gfx.teamBattle.fallLine: Short line when the posting team lost. {team} is the team's name.
gfx.teamBattle.setCount: In the facts line; {count} is the number of sets. A 'set' is one best-of-3 match between two players.
gfx.teamBattle.winner: Small label on the winning team's line; often in capitals.
gfx.teamBattle.set: Small column label between the two team names (the score of each set).
gfx.teamBattle.defeated: Ghost Pixels style: a battle-message line, imitating the old games. {team} is the opposing team's name.
gfx.teamBattle.won: Ghost Pixels style battle-message line. {team} is the winning team; the scores are separated by a hyphen.
gfx.teamBattle.blackedOut: Ghost Pixels style battle-message line, imitating the old games' losing message. {team} is the posting team.
gfx.comicRef.vs: Between the two sides on a comic poster; printed in capitals.
gfx.comicRef.win: Comic poster tab for a win. Must fit a narrow tab: max 6 characters.
gfx.comicRef.final: Comic poster tab for a loss. Must fit a narrow tab: max 6 characters.
gfx.day2.record: Shown when the player has no record entered; a label for the record bar.
gfx.day2.recordN: Record bar when the record is a number like 7-2; {record} is that record.
gfx.day2.title.regionals: Top-bar title when no event name is typed.
gfx.day2.title.play: Top-bar title when no event name is typed.
gfx.day2.title.internationals: Top-bar title when no event name is typed.
gfx.day2.title.special: Top-bar title when no event name is typed.
gfx.day2.title.worlds: Top-bar title when no event name is typed.
gfx.wide.results: Tag in the header of the landscape layouts; often in capitals.
gfx.wide.theTopN: Kicker on the Editorial Top 4 columns layout; {count} is the number of players.
gfx.wide.winnerBurst: Comic starburst on 1st place. Must fit inside a starburst: max 10 characters.
gfx.wide.championBurst: Comic starburst on the champion. Must fit inside a starburst: max 12 characters.
gfx.wide.resultsBurst: Comic starburst in the header. Must fit inside a starburst: max 10 characters.
gfx.wide.topBurst: Comic starburst in the header; {count} is the number of players.
gfx.wide.no: Ghost Pixels window title: the placing as a Pokédex-like number, e.g. No.1.
gfx.comicRef.winsLine: Second line of the yellow WINS strip on the Comic Book Poster (Replay) when the winner's name is too long for one line: line 1 is the name, line 2 is this word. Short names use "{name} wins" on one line instead.
ui.home.metaDescription: Home page (mismatched.gg): the description search engines and link previews show. Not visible on the page.
ui.home.tagline: Home page: line under the Mismatched logo at the top; printed in capitals.
ui.home.graphics.title: Home page: title of the card that links to the graphics generator; printed in capitals.
ui.home.graphics.kicker: Home page: small line under the Graphics Generator card title; printed in capitals.
ui.home.graphics.description: Home page: Graphics Generator card text. Champions = the game Pokémon Champions; .tdf = the TOM tournament file.
ui.home.graphics.previewAlt: Home page: description of the example graphic on the Graphics Generator card, read by screen readers (not shown).
ui.home.graphics.go: Home page: button on the Graphics Generator card; printed in capitals.
ui.home.invitational.kicker: Home page: small line under the DMV Invitational card title; printed in capitals.
ui.home.invitational.description: Home page: DMV Invitational card text.
ui.home.invitational.loading: Home page: shown on the DMV Invitational card while the live standings load; printed in capitals.
ui.home.invitational.live: Home page: above the live top 5 on the DMV Invitational card. {count} = how many players have points. Printed in capitals.
ui.home.invitational.unavailable: Home page: shown instead of the top 5 when the standings can't be loaded (the card still links to the full page). Printed in capitals.
ui.home.invitational.cut: Home page: under the live top 5. {cut} = how many players are invited (24). Printed in capitals.

ui.home.invitational.points.note: Home page: after each player's points in the live top 5 ("224 PTS"). Abbreviation of points.

ui.home.invitational.go: Home page: button on the DMV Invitational card; printed in capitals.
ui.home.calendar.title: Home page: title of the Calendar card; printed in capitals.
ui.home.calendar.kicker: Home page: small line under the Calendar card title; printed in capitals.
ui.home.calendar.description: Home page: Calendar card text (the calendar isn't built yet).
ui.home.calendar.soon: Home page: label on the Calendar card until it's built; printed in capitals.
ui.home.kofi.title: Home page: heading of the Ko-fi (donations) panel under the cards. Mismatched is the site's name.
ui.home.kofi.text: Home page: text in the Ko-fi (donations) panel. Ko-fi is the tipping website (a name, not translated).
ui.home.kofi.go: Home page: button that opens Mismatched's Ko-fi page; printed in capitals.
ui.home.footer.legal: Home page: small print at the bottom. Company names stay as written.
